standard_prerequisites.name: Torsors under the units of the structure sheaf and their classification by H^1
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma labelled lemma-torsors-h1 (source line 268, Stacks tag 02FQ, counted earlier in this night's work); invoked at proof lines 444-445
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the bijection between O_X^*-torsors and H^1(X, O_X^*), which is what makes it enough to prove injectivity and surjectivity of the map built in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: A torsor is trivial exactly when it has a global section
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemma labelled lemma-trivial-torsor (source line 256, Stacks tag 02FP); invoked at proof lines 451-452
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the injectivity step, i.e. that a trivial associated torsor means the invertible sheaf is free.

core_obligations: Build the map from invertible sheaves to torsors: for an invertible O_X-module L consider the presheaf L^* of sections s such that multiplication by s is an isomorphism, verify the sheaf condition, the simply transitive action of O_X^* by multiplication and the existence of sections locally, and conclude that L^* is an O_X^*-torsor, giving a map from invertible sheaves up to isomorphism to O_X^*-torsors up to isomorphism, which the author does not check to be a homomorphism (proof lines 416-443).
Reduce to bijectivity: by the torsor-H^1 classification the target is H^1(X, O_X^*), so only injectivity and surjectivity of that map remain to be shown (proof lines 444-448).

Injectivity and surjectivity: if L^* is trivial then it has a global section, which forces L to be free and gives injectivity; conversely, from an O_X^*-torsor F one forms the presheaf L_1 = (F x O_X)/O_X^* with the O_X-module structure described by (s, g) + (s', g') = (s, g + (s'/s)g'), sheafifies to L, and obtains the associated torsor L^* = F, which the author leaves to the reader (proof lines 450-473).
proof_roadmap: Associate to an invertible sheaf its sheaf of nondegenerate sections and observe that it is an O_X^*-torsor (proof lines 416-442).
Use the torsor classification to reduce the statement to injectivity and surjectivity of that association (proof lines 444-448).
Prove injectivity by the trivial-torsor criterion and surjectivity by the explicit quotient presheaf construction and its sheafification (proof lines 450-473).
difficulty_reason: The lemma identifies H^1(X, O_X^*) with the Picard group of a ringed space all of whose stalks are local rings (statement lines 407-411). As in its site-theoretic sibling the proof has to build the dictionary in both directions: an invertible sheaf is sent to its sheaf of nondegenerate sections, which needs the sheaf condition, a simply transitive action and local existence of sections, and conversely an O_X^*-torsor is turned into an invertible module through the quotient presheaf (F x O_X)/O_X^* with the action (s, g) -> (fs, f^{-1}g) and its sheafification (proof lines 416-473). The hypothesis on stalks is what makes the word invertible meaningful here. The author leaves two verifications to the reader, including that the composites are the identity; both sentences are reproduced as written. The claim is H2.
